title: Chapter 81 — The Economics of the Attach
intro: The margin architecture of appliance retail and the arithmetic that makes the ticket — not the product — the real business.

sections.title: The Product Is Not the Profit
sections.content:
In appliance retail, the margin on the appliance itself is often thin. The real profitability comes from the attach: delivery, installation, haul-away, accessories, protection plans, and financing.

A $2,500 refrigerator sale at 18% margin generates $450. Add delivery, installation, haul-away, a protection plan, and a water filter — the ticket becomes $3,200 and the margin doubles. The attach is where the business actually makes money.

sections.title: Every Line Matters
sections.content:
Delivery, installation, and haul-away are services the customer needs. Protection plans cover their investment. Accessories complete the purchase. Financing makes it affordable.

None of these should be treated as optional add-ons. They are part of the complete solution. Present them that way — as value, not upsells.

sections.title: Coaching Rule
sections.content:
When evaluating attach rate, ask:

Does the salesperson present the complete ticket — or just the product price?
Do they explain each attachment as value — or apologize for the cost?
Is the store's attach rate improving — or flat?
Does the team understand the margin architecture — or just focus on the product sale?
